summary: This is a Terminal component that displays shell commands and output with optional typewriter animation. It extracts text from React children (including MDX headings), handles animated character-by-character typing for command lines while instantly showing output lines, and provides a copy button that can optionally extract only the commands. The animation only starts when the terminal scrolls into view and can be skipped by clicking.

explanations.33: This defines a type alias for a Map that associates React element types (like heading functions from MDX) with their corresponding prefix strings (like '# ' for h1).
explanations.38: The separator parameter defaults to '\n' but gets overridden to an empty string when recursing into Fragment children, so substituted variable values don't get spurious line breaks attached.
explanations.43: This recursively calls getCopyText on each array item and joins them with the separator, building up the full text representation of nested React elements.
explanations.51: We're casting the child object to ReactElement because we already checked it's an object, but TypeScript doesn't know that yet without the explicit cast.
explanations.55: If the element is a Fragment, we use an empty separator for its children to avoid adding line breaks between inline substituted tokens; otherwise we use '\n' for normal elements.
explanations.64: This function returns different animation speeds depending on how many lines of output there are, so short terminals animate quickly while long ones don't feel slow.
explanations.152: We capture the animated lines only once when typewriter becomes true, not keeping them live, so if a user edits variables mid-animation the in-flight animation completes with the original text.
explanations.177: We create an IntersectionObserver to detect when this terminal component scrolls into the user's viewport before starting the animation.
explanations.206: The regex checks if a line starts with whitespace followed by $ or #, which indicates it's a command line rather than output.
explanations.209: On command lines, we advance one character at a time using the effectiveSpeed delay; on output lines we skip this and jump to the next line after a pause.
explanations.214: Empty lines get a shorter pause (80ms) than regular output lines (effectiveDelay), so the animation flows naturally without lingering on blank space.
explanations.240: We extract the text to copy from resolvedChildren, which already has variable substitutions applied.
explanations.242: When copyCommandOnly is true, we filter to only command lines (those starting with $ or #) and strip off the prompt prefix so the user gets text they can directly paste.
explanations.265: This calculates the partially-typed current line by taking only the first charIdx characters, or an empty string if we haven't reached this line yet.
explanations.276: When animating, the cursor changes to pointer and a title appears, signaling to the user they can click to skip the animation.
